title: Dead to Sin, Alive to God

reflections.title: "No Longer Slaves to Sin"

reflect.text: When Jesus died on the cross, our old sinful life was put to death with Him. This means sin has lost its ruling authority over our daily choices. Too often, believers still live like frightened prisoners trapped in a cage. Yet God gives us the capacity through His grace, His loving and undeserved kindness, to walk out of that trap. Christian maturity means we stop making excuses and boldly welcome the freedom Christ won for us.

Why would we ever want to go back to our old captivity? Sin always promises satisfaction, but it only delivers lies and brings deep sorrow. As Charles Spurgeon wrote, "Christians can never sin cheaply," because disobedience destroys our peace of mind, clouds our friendship with Jesus, and hinders our prayers. If you have stumbled today, do not stay away in shame. Turn straight back to Jesus, knowing His grace and forgiving love are ready to receive you.

questions: Are you living like someone who has been set free, or are you still obeying sin as if it were your master?
When you stumble, what helps you turn quickly back to Jesus rather than hiding in guilt?
reflections.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for breaking the power of sin when You died for us on the cross. Help us to stop making excuses and to walk boldly in the freedom You purchased. Whenever we wander or make mistakes, remind us of Your gentle love and draw our hearts quickly back to You. Amen.

reflections.title: "Dead to Sin, Alive to God"

reflect.text: Jesus truly rose from the dead in real history, and because we are united with Him, our standing has changed forever. We no longer have to let the world dictate how we think or search for value in worldly approval. Instead, we know that Christ has the power to transform anyone, no matter how deep their past rebellion was. Being alive to God means we can practice walking in close, daily communion with Him in every situation.

Living as someone alive to God also means making a conscious choice about who directs our lives. Sin wants to rule over us and ruin us, while God desires to bless us with life. F. B. Meyer wrote that we must "turn to God with a full purpose of heart" and give Him complete possession of our minds, voices, and hands. Along with offering ourselves to God, we protect our hearts by avoiding tempting habits and leaning on prayer, Scripture, and our church family.

questions: What parts of your life, such as your words or your thoughts, can you hand over to God today?
What tempting situations or habits do you need to avoid with the help of prayer and Christian friends?
reflections.prayer: Heavenly Father, we thank You that Jesus is alive and that we are alive to You through Him. Take our minds, our hands, and our voices so that they can be used for Your good purposes. Give us wisdom to turn away from temptation and help us stay close to You and our fellow believers. Amen.

reflections.title: Free Under the Power of Grace

reflect.text: Sin is an ambitious enemy that always tries to claim the throne of our hearts. At times, we might look at our weaknesses and fear that our old faults will conquer us completely. Yet God gives us a comforting promise in this passage. Sin may attack us and even wound us, but it will never establish its rule over us again.

The reason sin cannot master us is that we live under grace, God's unearned favor, rather than under the law. If we were under the law, our failures would only leave us trapped and powerless. Instead, we are sheltered by God's promise. His grace constantly restores us when we wander, cleanses our impurities, and snaps the chains of bad habits.

Because the Lord has made us free, we do not have to live like exhausted slaves working desperately to earn eternal life. We can take courage to fight against our daily temptations. We do not face this struggle alone, because God Himself gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

questions: When you feel discouraged by your struggles, how does knowing you live under grace give you comfort?
How does being free from having to earn God's love give you courage to stand against temptation?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, thank You for placing us under Your grace, where sin no longer has authority over our lives. When our weaknesses frighten us, remind us of Your promise to hold us fast and heal our wounds. Grant us courage to battle temptation each day, trusting that the victory belongs to You through Christ. Amen.
